description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number of biomedical entities and the accuracy (ACC %) of various model editing methods, as evaluated in the context of long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 25% to 60%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 30%, 40%, 50%, and 60%. Six distinct methods are plotted: Base (black solid line with circular markers) starts at ~28% ACC and increases slightly to ~32%; FT (blue solid line with downward-pointing triangular markers) begins at ~32% and rises to ~38%; IKE (red solid line with upward-pointing triangular markers) starts at ~33% and climbs to ~41%; MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers) begins at ~36%, rises to ~45%, and plateaus; MEMIT (purple solid line with pentagonal markers) starts at ~36%, increases to ~46%, and then stabilizes; and ROME (green solid line with square markers) begins at ~43%, rises steeply to ~57%, and continues to climb slightly beyond 10³. All lines show non-decreasing trends, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers.
